clue.text: Master of some art

parts.note: the whole clue describes a distinguished practitioner, especially a great conductor or composer of music

explanation.walkthrough: A plain cryptic definition: the vagueness of 'some art' hides that the art in question is usually music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title is given to an eminent musician or conductor, a master of the art of music.

clue.text: Curse child from African country

parts.note: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Someone lays a curse on a youngster who comes from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: the country comes before the child although the clue names the child first.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a malediction, the opposite of a benison or blessing.

clue.text: Abstraction in the finish will get you transported

indicators.note: the word in tells us the abstraction sits within the finish

parts.note: the finish of something is its end
abstraction in the sense of a dreamy, absent state of mind, a trance

explanation.surface: Daydreaming at the end of the race leaves a runner carried away.
explanation.definitionFit: Transported in the sense of carried away with delight, rapt or spellbound.

clue.text: Taking time to overturn this treasure?

annotationWithheld.why: Taking time to overturn this treasure? (5): the wordplay is T plus an anagram of OVER, with 'turn' as the indicator, so the single word 'overturn' supplies both the fodder and the anagram signal, a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Taking time to overturn this treasure?

clue.text: Something putrefying close by, must surely do so

definitions.text: Something putrefying close by, must surely do so

parts.note: food that is going rotten is said to be off
close as a noun, the end or conclusion

explanation.surface: Rotting rubbish nearby is bound to upset the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: something rotten nearby will certainly upset people, 'do so' standing for the verb the answer gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotting smell nearby is sure to cause displeasure or affront the nose of anyone near it.

clue.text: Top and tail, perhaps? That's fine

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word tail might be arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Asked whether trimming both ends will do, someone replies that it is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top and tail' looks like the cooking phrase for trimming vegetables, but 'perhaps' is an anagram signal working on 'tail' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital! is a dated British exclamation of approval meaning excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Riches he amassed from cheese

indicators.note: amassed suggests the letters are gathered up and heaped together in a new order

explanation.surface: A man has piled up a fortune from the dairy trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly English cheese named after the county in north-west England where it originated.

clue.text: Bird peering around has eagle's head

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of peering are moved about into a new order

parts.note: the printed word peering has one R; the setter's fodder needs a second R to make the nine letters

indicators.note: the head of the word eagle's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bird looking about has the head of an eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: PEERING with E (the first letter of 'eagle's') rearranged by 'around' gives only eight letters; the setter's fodder lacks the second R that the nine-letter answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A large falcon, famous for its high-speed stooping dive on prey.

clue.text: Land in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone owns a plot of land somewhere around the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for earth or ground, used in English for dry land as in terra firma.

clue.text: An oil is deployed in this connection

indicators.note: deployed suggests the letters are spread out and set in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Lubricant is applied to a mechanical joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A link or close working relationship between people or groups, also an affair.

clue.text: Excuses for fires?

definitions.meaning: to excuse someone is to spare them punishment or duty
to fire a gun or a firework is to discharge it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both pardons someone from a penalty and discharges a gun or firework.

clue.text: Twisted route dropping round, drowned valley to ancient country

indicators.note: twisted suggests the remaining letters of route are wrung into a new order
dropping says a letter is let fall from the word route

parts.note: a round shape, a ring, looks like the letter O
a ria is a long inlet formed when a river valley is flooded by the sea

explanation.surface: A winding road, skipping a bend, leads past a flooded valley into an old land.
explanation.walkthrough: A ria is a coastal inlet made by the sea flooding a river valley; 'round' is the letter O dropped before the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient region of central Italy inhabited by the Etruscans, roughly modern Tuscany.

clue.text: At sea, as gannet shrieks, lurking danger becomes apparent

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Over the waves, a screeching seabird warns of some hidden menace.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a treacherous person or a hidden threat, from Virgil's lurking serpent.

clue.text: Metal of small value in America

definitions.meaning: the US five-cent coin, a coin of small value

explanation.definitionFit: A hard metallic element and also the American five-cent coin made from an alloy containing it.

clue.text: Tend, perhaps, to hold point of view that's complicated

indicators.note: to hold says the first piece contains the second
perhaps suggests the word tend in some other arrangement

parts.note: an angle is a particular point of view on a matter

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to stick to a viewpoint ends up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tend, perhaps' reads like an example of a verb, but 'perhaps' is the anagram signal and 'to hold' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled up or involved, as in a convoluted plot or situation.

clue.text: Fulfilment achieved — if turn round, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the printed words if turn give one I; the fodder needs a second I, as if the clue read if I turn
a round shape, a ring, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Success comes if you just turn things around.
explanation.walkthrough: IF TURN plus O (from 'round') rearranged by 'maybe' gives seven letters, not eight: the second I is missing, as if the setter meant 'if I turn round'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to fruition means a plan being realised, its completion or achievement.

clue.text: Intimate random parking in it can make you annoyed by delay

indicators.note: random suggests the letters are mixed up haphazardly

parts.note: P is the standard map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Being unable to find a parking space near your date makes you irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: INTIMATE and P are rearranged together by 'random'; 'in it can make you' is padding linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless and irritated at having to wait, the state of someone who cannot bear hold-ups.

clue.text: Become pale and weak? Raise spirits, holding it up, love

indicators.note: holding says the first piece contains the others

parts.note: to elate is to make cheerful, raise the spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Feeling washed out, someone tries to cheer themselves up with love.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads a word bottom to top; love is O from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a plant grown without light, to turn pale and spindly; of a person, to lose vigour.

clue.text: Think to act as a medium in a short time

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to mediate is to act as a go-between or medium
T is the short form, the abbreviation, for time

explanation.surface: A psychic thinks about a quick séance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect deeply or contemplate, especially in quiet concentration.

clue.text: They may explain why it rises and travels around

indicators.note: around says the travelling word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to move is to travel from place to place

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the word it is read upwards

explanation.surface: A detective asks what makes something go up and go round.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' reads a word bottom to top; the definition is the whole of 'They may explain why'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasons behind an action, especially what a detective looks for to account for a crime.

clue.text: Moderate one's mood

definitions.meaning: to moderate is to soften or tone down
a person's state of mind or humour

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to tone down or mitigate; as a noun a frame of mind, as in a good one.

clue.text: Change, as it were, and put right

definitions.meaning: change in the sense of putting on different clothes, read as dressing again
to remedy or set right a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two parts it suggests putting clothes on again; as one word it means to remedy a grievance.

clue.text: Business matter involving time and trouble

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: trouble suggests the word and is disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A commercial deal takes ages and causes difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' tempts as ADO, which gives nothing here: it is the signal to scramble 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items of business to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: After dark no gent goes out, it's assumed

indicators.note: goes out suggests the letters are taken apart and set in another order

explanation.surface: Once night falls no man leaves the house, so it is supposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepted as true without question, presumed without any proof.

clue.text: Fencing for the lad to fix

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name, here any lad
to do something can mean to arrange or fix it, as in doing someone's hair

explanation.surface: A youngster needs fencing put up to mend a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese martial art of fighting with bamboo swords, a form of fencing.

clue.text: Dam built by a bird

parts.note: a swan is a large water bird

explanation.surface: A water bird has constructed a barrier across a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: The great dam across the Nile in southern Egypt, named after the nearby city.

clue.text: Everyone in a civic centre rejected this sort of icecream

indicators.note: rejected means the whole phrase is thrown back and read in reverse

parts.note: everyone together is all

indicators.note: the centre of the word civic is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Everybody at a town hall turned down this flavour of ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but supplies its own two letters; 'rejected' sends the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The plain, standard flavour of ice cream made with the orchid-pod spice.

clue.text: Has arrived, or can't be found?

definitions.meaning: split into words it says someone is present at this moment

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it says someone is present at this moment; whole it means in no place at all.

clue.text: Notice each side of the pool -—a metrical foot

indicators.note: each side of says the notice is split to flank the pool

parts.note: to see is to notice
a pond is a small pool of water

explanation.surface: Signs are posted on both sides of the swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of verse made of two long or stressed syllables in succession.

clue.text: See revenue from girl set off

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: off suggests the word set goes awry and is rearranged

explanation.surface: Income comes from a girl who has set off.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is a bishop's diocese; ANNA is followed by TES, the word 'set' rearranged by 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the first year's income of a benefice, paid by a new incumbent to the Pope.
